stories.title: Dublin man transformed after new heart procedure at Mater
stories.summary: A man has described as "black and white" his transformation after undergoing a new heart procedure at the Mater Hospital in Dublin. The hospital described the procedure as a "major advancement in cardiac care" which it can now carry out for patients who are considered too high-risk for conventional open-heart surgery. Derek Toomey from Finglas in Dublin was diagnosed in 2023 with a severely narrowed, calcified mitral valve. He had been suffering from low energy and loss of breath, with the simplest of tasks becoming a challenge.

stories.summary: The European Union intends to significantly expand sanctions against Russia ⁠in the coming months, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has said. In July, the EU approved its most ⁠recent sanctions package against Russia over its war in Ukraine, imposing curbs on the country's banking sector and cryptocurrency networks. The bloc has adopted 21 rounds of sanctions against Russia since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. "EU sanctions have already cost Russia dearly, depriving Russia's war machine of over €1 trillion and for autumn ‌I am ⁠putting forward the most far-reaching sanctions listings since the start of the war," she told German daily newspaper Die Welt.

stories.title: Annual house price growth eases to 5.6% in June - CSO
stories.summary: The rate of growth in house prices slowed in the year to June, according to the latest figures from the Central Statistics Office. The figures, from the CSO's national Residential Property Price Index (RPPI), show that in 12 months to June this year, the average price of a home rose by 5.6% - compared to 6.1% in the year to May. The annual increase in residential property prices of 5.6% for June was the lowest annual rise since January 2024. House price inflation has been gradually moderating from the most recent year-on-year peak of 10.1% in August 2024.

stories.title: Evacuation orders lifted in Belgian wildfire zone
stories.summary: Authorities in Belgium and Germany lifted the last remaining evacuation orders in the border region where firefighters appeared to be gaining the upper hand against the massive High Fens wildfire. After being grounded by bad weather, water-dropping aircraft were back out helping to quell Belgium's largest wildfire in a century, after fire crews hacked their way through boggy terrain overnight to fully "encircle" the blaze. Crisis cell spokesman Tony Hosmans said the fire burning since Friday "has been contained and should no longer be able to spread" - after threatening to spill over the German border to the east. New flare-ups were still emerging across the vast site - with the blaze smouldering underground in the peaty soil - but were being "brought under control" one by one, he said, with the next goal to finally tame the fire.

stories.summary: Ireland women's hockey captain Sarah Hawkshaw believes that all the pressure is on Belgium ahead of their crucial World Cup Pool C decider. A 3-2 victory over New Zealand on Tuesday keeps Ireland's qualification hopes alive. With the top two teams going through to the second round, Ireland must get a win against tournament hosts Belgium to avoid the 9th–16th classification games. Ireland will be the underdogs going into the game in front of a partisan Belgian crowd in Wavre, and they narrowly lost two Pro League games 2-1 to them in Dublin last December.

The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. stories.title: FIFA sacking Lamour sends 'troubling message' - UEFA VP
stories.summary: FIFA's decision to dismiss senior executive Kevin Lamour sends a "deeply troubling message to all of us seeking change", UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister has said. FIFA confirmed Lamour’s departure as chief operating officer on Monday evening, just over two weeks after he released a statement to the Associated Press saying the FIFA administration had been "deceived" by president Gianni Infantino over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors. Lamour’s statement on 31 July, along with the resignation of senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro earlier the same day, heaped further pressure on Infantino, with Lamour describing the private investor plan as "the project of one person". Now UEFA executive committee member McAllister, a former Wales captain who worked with Lamour at European football’s governing body when he was its deputy general secretary, has spoken out to criticise his sacking.

stories.title: Debut tries for Flood, Murphy as Leinster defeat Connacht
stories.summary: Debut tries from Stacey Flood and Niamh Murphy helped Leinster to overcome Connacht 36-21 for their opening Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship win. Having failed to pick up a point against Munster, this was a must-win game for Leinster at Energia Park, and they prevailed thanks to closing scores from Maggie Boylan and replacement Murphy. Craig Hansberry's young Connacht side led early on, and twice closed the gap to three points, but they are now a point behind second-placed Leinster, in the table, heading into the final round. Leinster's improved performance in front of their home support had them 17-14 ahead at half-time, with Boylan, Hannah Wilson, and Emma Tilly all touching down.

stories.title: Mean Girls: How Tina Fey's teen classic became a cultural icon
stories.summary: Teenagers of the 80s had the oeuvre of filmmaker John Hughes to school them through the most painful moments of their adolescence. Teens in the 90s had pop adaptations of classics like Clueless (based on Jane Austen's Emma) or Ten Things I Hate About You (a sexy version of Shakespeare’s The Taming of the Shrew). For those coming of age in the early naughties, however, there was only one film in town: Mean Girls, the movie that launched the career of its stars Lindsay Lohan and Rachel McAdams, as well as its writer and co-star Tina Fey. I had already finished college when Mean Girls was released, but its anatomisation of the rigid social hierarchies were recognisable - and cathartically appealing - to anyone who had survived the brutal years of adolescence since teenagehood was first recognised in popular culture, in the post-World War Two period. Tina Fey herself was in her 30s when she wrote Mean Girls, catapulting her from small-screen supporting roles on and off the Saturday Night Live circuit into the glaring limelight of Hollywood. Formally, the film was an adaptation of a popular self-help title, Queen Bees and Wannabes by Rosalind Wiseman, which was written as a supportive guide for parents navigating the dangerous playground of the middle years with their teenagers, but Fey also drew heavily on her own experience of high school in Pennsylvania in the 1980s. The intermittent voiceover, narrated by Lohan, who plays Cady - a homeschooled maths-whizz who finds herself thrown headfirst into the savage ecosystem of her peers when she enrols in her local high school - might well be the voice of Fey herself.

stories.summary: Laura Fitzachary is a historian and historical content creator based in Dublin who specialises in fashion and beauty history in Ireland and beyond. With a focus on health, natural beauty and minimalism (albeit through the skewed lens of Western beauty standards...), the 'clean girl aesthetic' appeared in 2020, becoming a lifestyle trend enthusiastically endorsed and proliferated on social media, particularly TikTok. You'll no doubt have seen versions of it: the dewy skin, the glossy blush, the barely there mascara and impeccably groomed brows, all topped off with a shiny slicked-back bun.

Following the inspection, HIQA notified both the HSE and Tusla of its concern. The inspection, which occurred in April, followed a cautionary meeting with the provider the previous month due to medicine management practices and other issues.

stories.title: Oil hovers near 3-week high on uncertainty over Hormuz
stories.summary: Oil prices trimmed gains but kept near a three-week high hit earlier today on uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and other ongoing supply disruptions in the market. Brent crude futures were up 18 cents, or 0.2%, at $91.20 this afternoon, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were 16 cents, or 0.19% higher at $85.10 a barrel. Brent crude hit its highest level since July 30, and WTI reached its highest since July 31 earlier in the session, before retreating. "Risk appetite received a boost following the announcement from the (Federal Reserve) increasing Treasury buybacks. The news saw the dollar tumble around 0.5% making the drop (in oil prices) even stronger in other currencies," Saxo Bank analyst Ole Hansen said.

stories.title: Conference League: Crunch time for Shamrock Rovers
stories.summary: Dublin's long, hot summer is fizzling out. It'll be grey and rainy tonight though still mild, with highest temperatures of 15 to 20 degrees and moderate winds. As we head towards late August, Stephen Bradley's men are top of the SSE Airtricity Men's Premier Division and still in Europe, but expectations are high in Tallaght, and events over the last seven days have led to some soul searching. It started with a dreadful performance in Albania. The Hoops took a 3-1 first-leg lead to Egnatia in their Europa League third-round qualification clash and imploded on the road, slumping to a 5-1 loss that was not at all flattering to the hosts. On Sunday, they raced into a two-goal lead against St Pat's in their Club Orange FAI Cup last-16 showdown at Richmond Park after making eight changes. It looked like Bradley was going to get a welcome tonic but Pat's rose off the canvas to force extra-time and ultimately swing the tie thanks to a winner from 17-year-old Sam Rooney.

stories.summary: Croke Park chiefs are keen to make Premier League pre-season friendlies like Wednesday night's clash between Manchester United and Leeds regular events. The match between the long-standing rivals was the first game of soccer to be played at the home of the GAA since 2009, but was seen as a huge success as a sell-out crowd of 75,000 watched Manchester United beat their old rivals on penalties. The only previous times soccer had been played at the venue were between 2007 and 2009 when it served as the temporary home of the Republic of Ireland during the redevelopment of Lansdowne Road. But Peter McKenna, Croke Park’s stadium and commercial director, is keen to change that to find new revenue streams to put into the GAA.

stories.title: The best moments from this year's Rose of Tralee
stories.summary: It was a baton-twirling, nail hammering, Irish dancing couple of nights down in the Kingdom as we counted down to the winner of this year's Rose of Tralee. Here are the best bits of this year's event . . . . Everyone knows that proud Kerry man Dáithí Ó Sé is still smarting over Mayo's famous and historic victory over the Kingdom in July's All-Ireland final (as he said, "I still have a twitch in my eye") and Carolina Rose, 28-year-old Grace O'Halloran, teased him about it in the nicest way possible on Tuesday night. Asked to sing one of the songs she had learnt since arriving in Ireland, she immediately burst into The Green and Red of Mayo. Dáithí looked on with a sporting smile, only for James Patrice to wheel on the Sam Maguire cup itself. "You’re killing me," cried Dáithí, before turning to Sam and saying, "I love you, I love you! Please come back to us." Toronto Rose Kylie Paliani is a very talented young lady - she has a degree in biochemical engineering and is a very skilled Irish dancer who has attended no less than 11 World Championships. However, she also proved that she has a possibly record-breaking talent for outfit changes. Kylie slipped out of her glittering floor-length blue gúna in 14 seconds to appear back on stage in a fetching pink and green Irish Dancing get-up for a quick once around the parlour. She also had some wise words for the watching world: "You don't have to give up your dreams to pursue your career, and you don't have to give up your career to pursue your dreams."

stories.title: Dublin's newest street mural honours the women of the Monto
stories.summary:
In a side street off Talbot St, a vibrant new mural is shedding light on the women of Monto, once one of Europe's largest red-light districts during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, bringing to life a rich but often forgotten part of Dublin's history. Muralist Holly Pereira has painted the striking artwork on Mabbot Lane, a small section of street that features in James Joyce's Ulysses, described as "the entrance to Nighttown". I have been practising as a muralist for 11 years, having worked as an illustrator before that. The first big mural I painted was coming up to Repeal the 8th referendum in 2016. From that moment, I was hooked on the scale, vibrancy and potential for communication within murals.

stories.title: UK inflation picks up after July surge in energy bills
stories.summary: A jump in household energy bills pushed British inflation to a four-month high in July, matching forecasts, and it looks set to rise further as the war in Iran grinds on with no end in sight. Annual consumer price inflation rose to 2.9% in July from a 15-month low of 2.6% in June, the Office for National Statistics said today, reflecting a 13% rise last month in the maximum tariff UK regulators allow energy firms to charge households. Economists polled by Reuters had widely expected to see a rise in inflation to 2.9%, although the Bank of England predicted a smaller rise to 2.8% in forecasts published at the end of last month and sees inflation peaking at 3.2% later this year. The data help explain new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's continuation of his predecessor's focus on reducing cost-of-living pressures on UK households, although stretched public finances before the government's annual budget in October offer little room for broad assistance.

Fresh from getting Arsenal over the line to their first league title in more than two decades, Arteta is now the elder statesman of the league after Pep Guardiola decided to call time on his 10 years with Manchester City. The next trick for Arteta is to defend the title and win back-to-back Premier Leagues for the first time in the club's history, surpassing even the achievements of Arsene Wenger. Arsenal go into the season as the heavy favourites. A sense of uncertainty and flux settles in over their rivals, while Arteta’s steady hand, long-term squad building and continued improvement means they’re the team to beat.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.
